name: input.position
description: Return the current cursor position in virtual-screen coordinates. Pass `include_monitor: true` to also return the index of the monitor the cursor is on (matches `system.info.screens[].index`). Per issue #69.

include_monitor.description: When true, the response includes a `monitor_index` field identifying the monitor under the cursor. Adds one `MonitorFromPoint` call per request. Default false keeps the typical-case payload minimal.

x.description: Cursor X in virtual-screen coordinates (DPI-aware on per-monitor-DPI-aware agents, matching `input.mouse.click` / `input.mouse.move` coordinate space).

monitor_index.description: 0-based monitor index from `system.info.screens[].index`. Present iff `include_monitor: true` was passed. The cursor's enclosing monitor; on NT 4 (single-monitor) always 0.

x-implementations.name: get_cursor_pos
x-implementations.description: Win32 `GetCursorPos`. Returns the cursor's screen position in DPI-virtualised coordinates on DPI-unaware agents, or virtual-screen pixels on per-monitor-DPI-aware agents (the modern agent default). When `include_monitor: true`, follows up with `MonitorFromPoint` + the agent's monitor-index table to report the index.

windows-modern.description: GetCursorPos in the agent's DPI awareness context. The agent runs as per-monitor-DPI-aware (DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2), so the returned coordinates are virtual-screen pixels matching the input.mouse.* coordinate space. `include_monitor: true` adds MonitorFromPoint(MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST) and looks the result up in the agent's monitor-handle-to-index table, which is rebuilt on display changes via WM_DISPLAYCHANGE.

windows-classic.description: GetCursorPos on NT 3.1+. Pre-NT-5, single-monitor only; `monitor_index` is always 0 with `include_monitor: true`. NT 5+ supports multi-monitor; the monitor lookup uses `MonitorFromPoint`.
